title: Flow-center alignment reduced the Ob-Yenisey peak excess by 72% in 30 certified years from 1936 to 1975, with mixed test support
abstract: We tested whether a flow-timing result from 1980-2011 transferred to a separate earlier record. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 daily flow at Ob-Salekhard and Yenisey-Igarka. Thirty complete certified years passed in a planned 1936-1979 window; the last retained year was 1975. Each April-August hydrograph had the same volume within its river. Aligning each flow center to its river mean reduced the mean seven-day peak excess over independent year pairing from 1,486 to 414 cubic metres per second. The reduction was 1,073, or 72.2%, with primary conditional permutation p = 0.0527. A refitted paired-year bootstrap range was 60 to 2,020; a three-position block range was 112 to 2,079. Five-year groups gave p = 0.1198; median-date alignment and circular shifts gave 0.0383 and 0.0061. Thus the point reduction transferred, but test support was mixed. This is a separate-period test on the same gauges and source, not proof of a cause or a coastal pulse. Sparse later coverage, source error, regulation, exchangeability and short blocks limit the result. Original code, aggregate evidence and fixed source hashes support reproduction.

display.caption: Peak excess over exact within-period year pairing, before and after flow-center alignment. Bars are point estimates. Tests and uncertainty are in the text.
